## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))

const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
mkdirSync('/tmp/gshots', { recursive: true })
const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 })
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
const errs = []
page.on('pageerror', e => { errs.push(e.message); console.log('PAGEERROR:', e.message) })
page.on('console', m => { if (m.type() === 'error') { errs.push(m.text()); console.log('CONSOLE:', m.text()) } })
await page.goto('http://localhost:3002/', { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60000 })
await page.waitForTimeout(2200)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/gshots/01-lobby.png' })
console.log('lobby shot')
await page.locator('#startBtn').click({ timeout: 15000 })
console.log('started')
await page.waitForTimeout(3500)
console.log('health:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__FREEFALL__.player.health), 'enemies:', await page.evaluate(() => window.__FREEFALL__.enemies.length))
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/gshots/02-game.png' })
// open mod menu
await page.keyboard.press('KeyM')
await page.waitForTimeout(700)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/gshots/03-modmenu.png' })
// enable all
await page.locator('#enableAll').click()
await page.waitForTimeout(400)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/gshots/04-modall.png' })
await page.locator('#modApply').click()
await page.waitForTimeout(800)
// aim down sights and fire

await page.mouse.down({ button: 'right' })
await page.waitForTimeout(600)
await page.mouse.down({ button: 'left' })
await page.waitForTimeout(700)
await page.mouse.up({ button: 'left' })
await page.mouse.up({ button: 'right' })
await page.waitForTimeout(500)
await page.screenshot({ path: '/tmp/gshots/05-aim.png' })

console.log('errors:', errs.length)
await browser.close()

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 3D open-world shooting game inspired by Free Fire, with lobby/start flow and a mod menu containing Hologram, Silent Aim, Auto Headshot, Aim Kill, and Aimbot.
- Deliver a polished, visually impressive original game (offline AI sandbox, not cheats for a live game).

## Requirements
- No clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them at completion.
- Include a lobby with a start option and a functional mod menu with the five named features.
- Must render and be playable in the browser; mobile support expected.
- Avoid using actual Free Fire trademarks/assets; build an original game.

## Decisions
- Created original title **FREEFALL — ISLAND OPS**, single-player offline AI sandbox.
- Built with Three.js r160 vendored locally; procedural terrain, buildings, vegetation, weapons, enemies, audio, and textures (no external game assets).
- Mod menu explicitly labeled sandbox/offline only.
- Implemented additional mods beyond request: Infinite Ammo, No Recoil, Wireframe, Overclock, God Mode, Bullet Time.
- Mod menu access via `M`/`Insert`, lobby button, pause menu, and touch button.
- Game modes: Solo Survival (20 kills) and Training Ground (endless respawns).

## Work State
### Completed
- Downloaded Three.js to `js/vendor/three.module.js`; fonts to `assets/fonts/`.
- Wrote `index.html`, `css/main.css`, `js/world.js`, `js/audio.js`, `js/game.js`.
- Lobby UI rendered successfully at desktop and mobile; screenshot captured.
- Start button now has `aria-label="Start Game"` so capture harness auto-click works.
- Game starts, renders terrain/buildings/palms/water/HUD/enemies/minimap/compass.
- Mod menu renders and is visually polished.
- Basic shooting, enemy AI, damage, pickups, zone, win/lose logic implemented.
- Fixed: enemy death animation `deathBaseY`, mobile controls `.hidden` removal, compass resolution, enemy LOS throttle, camera sync before firing, aim target caching, spawn grace, victory guard, spawn loop guard, weapon scale/tracer size.
- Server running on port 3002 via tmux session `freefall`; `default-capture.mjs` works after aria-label fix except current console error was fixed.

### Active
- Improving visual quality: viewmodel is still too blocky/large; scene feels flat/sparse.
- Improving performance (SwiftShader measured ~5 FPS at 1440x900; only 1 shot fired during 1.2s hold due to low FPS).
- Fixing mod switch checked styling: CSS `input:checked+span` does not apply despite `input.checked=true` and `:checked` matching; needs class-based toggle.
- Rewriting enemy model for merged geometry to reduce draw calls and add detail.
- Planning spawn relocation near village/market for a more impressive starting view.
- Need to verify mod features (Hologram/Silent Aim/Headshot/Aim Kill/Aimbot) actually work in play.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Fix mod menu switches by adding `.switch.on span` / `.switch.on span::before` CSS and toggling `label.classList.toggle('on', checked)` in `syncModUI()`.
2. Increase mod menu description readability (font size/contrast) and verify all tabs/feature toggles.
3. Rewrite `createEnemy()` using merged geometry helper to cut ~17 meshes/enemy to ~7–8 draw calls; add pouches, helmet rails, knee pads, boots, detailed gun.
4. Improve viewmodel: reduce optic cylinder size, add forearms/hands, lower-right placement, scale ~0.55, better silhouette.
5. Auto-detect SwiftShader/software renderer; set pixel ratio ~0.72–0.8, shadow map 1024, PCFShadowMap, disable leaf/bush/nut shadows, reduce terrain/water segments.
6. Relocate `world.spawn` near village/market (e.g., around `(-20,18)` facing market) and re-filter spawns.
7. Improve world visuals: stronger directional lighting/contrast, grass tufts, distant islands/haze, sun lens flare, more ambient props.
8. Test firing/aimbot/silent aim/holo/headshot/aimkill via Playwright and take fresh screenshots.

## Relevant Files
- `js/game.js`: main game loop, player, weapons, enemies, HUD, mod menu, input, game flow.
- `js/world.js`: procedural island, terrain, buildings, vegetation, water, sky, colliders, spawns, pickups, lighting.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural WebAudio engine.
- `index.html`: lobby, HUD, mod menu, settings, pause/result, mobile markup.
- `css/main.css`: full UI styling, responsive/mobile, mod menu.
- `js/vendor/three.module.js`: Three.js r160.
- `assets/fonts/`: Rajdhani/Orbitron woff2 files.
- `README.md`: project publishing references.
- `/tmp/shots*`, `/tmp/gshots`: screenshots from testing.
- `/tmp/test-game.mjs`, `/tmp/debug-game.mjs`, `/tmp/debug2.mjs`: Playwright test scripts.
- `/tmp/freefall-server.log`: dev server log.

## Important Context
- Serve with tmux: `PORT=3002 node "$RUNTIME_DIR/scripts/default-start.mjs"`; session name `freefall`.
- Playwright launch config: `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json`; software rendering likely SwiftShader.
- Capture harness auto-clicks button with aria-label or exact text `Start Game`; keep `aria-label="Start Game"`.
- Measured ~5 FPS under SwiftShader; optimize for capture/playability.
- Mod switches currently computed style stays unchecked; class-based fix required.
- Use `window.__FREEFALL__` for debugging: exposes `game, player, enemies, MODS, world, camera, startGame`.
- 404 in console is likely `favicon.ico` only.

```js
function mergeColored(parts) {
  // parts: {geo, color, pos:[x,y,z], rot:[rx,ry,rz], scale}
  let arrays = { position: [], normal: [], uv: [], color: [] }
  const c = new THREE.Color()
  for (const p of parts) {
    let g = p.geo.index ? p.geo.toNonIndexed() : p.geo.clone()
    const m = new THREE.Matrix4().compose(
      new THREE.Vector3(...p.pos),
      new THREE.Quaternion().setFromEuler(new THREE.Euler(...(p.rot||[0,0,0]))),
      new THREE.Vector3(...(p.scale||[1,1,1]))
    )
    g.applyMatrix4(m)
    const pos = g.attributes.position.array, nor = g.attributes.normal.array
    arrays.position.push(...pos); arrays.normal.push(...nor)
    // uv may not exist? BoxGeometry/SphereGeometry have uv.
    if (g.attributes.uv) arrays.uv.push(...g.attributes.uv.array)
    const n = g.attributes.position.count
    c.setHex(p.color)
    for (let i=0;i<n;i++) arrays.color.push(c.r,c.g,c.b)
    g.dispose()
  }
  const out = new THREE.BufferGeometry()
  out.setAttribute('position', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(arrays.position,3))
  out.setAttribute('normal', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(arrays.normal,3))
  out.setAttribute('uv', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(arrays.uv,2)) // uv length matches positions if all have uv
  out.setAttribute('color', new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(arrays.color,3))
  out.computeBoundingSphere()
  return out
}
```

 // ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── renderer / scene

-renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 1.6))
+// Detect software rasterisers (SwiftShader / llvmpipe) so the game stays playable
+// in CI, VMs and low-power devices instead of rendering millions of fill-rate heavy pixels.
+let softwareRenderer = false, gpuName = ''
+try {
+  const gl = renderer.getContext()
+  const ext = gl.getExtension('WEBGL_debug_renderer_info')
+  gpuName = ext ? String(gl.getParameter(ext.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL) || '') : ''
+  softwareRenderer = /swiftshader|llvmpipe|software|microsoft basic|mesa offscreen/i.test(gpuName)
+} catch (err) { /* renderer info unavailable */ }
+const basePixelRatio = softwareRenderer ? 0.72 : Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio || 1, 1.5)
+let currentPixelRatio = basePixelRatio
+renderer.setPixelRatio(currentPixelRatio)
 renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight)
 renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true

import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 })
const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width: 1440, height: 900 } })
await page.goto('http://localhost:3002/', { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 60000 })
await page.waitForTimeout(1500)
await page.locator('#startBtn').click({ timeout: 15000 })
await page.waitForTimeout(2500)
const fps = async (label) => {
  const v = await page.evaluate(() => new Promise(res => { let f=0; const t=performance.now(); const tick=()=>{f++; if(performance.now()-t<1600) requestAnimationFrame(tick); else res({fps:f/((performance.now()-t)/1000), info:{...window.__FREEFALL__.renderer.info.render}, pr: window.devicePixelRatio})}; requestAnimationFrame(tick) }))
  console.log(label, 'fps', v.fps.toFixed(1), 'calls', v.info.calls, 'tris', v.info.triangles, 'pr', v.pr)
}
await fps('baseline')
console.log('canvas', await page.evaluate(() => [document.querySelector('#game').width, document.querySelector('#game').height]))
await page.evaluate(() => { window.__FREEFALL__.renderer.shadowMap.enabled = false; window.__FREEFALL__.world.sun.castShadow = false })
await fps('no shadows')
await page.evaluate(() => { window.__FREEFALL__.enemies.forEach(e => e.group.visible = false) })
await fps('no enemies')
await page.evaluate(() => { window.__FREEFALL__.scene.children.forEach(c => { if (c.isMesh || c.isInstancedMesh || c.isGroup) c.visible = false }) })
await fps('empty scene')
await browser.close()
